property_summary: After seeding an empty market, the contract becomes initialized and thus allows getFreeKilo() to succeed (not revert) for an address with zero kilos.
After calling seedMarket when marketDrugs was zero, the contract should report initialized == true (so getMyKilo for a fresh user increases over 0 after time advances).
After seeding an empty market, the contract must become initialized so that subsequent calls requiring initialization (e.g., getFreeKilo) can succeed (do not revert).

After seeding an empty market, the contract's initialized flag becomes true, so a subsequent call that requires initialized (sellDrugs) will revert in the mutant but succeed (not revert) in the original — therefore calling a public view that depends on initialized (getMyDrugs via getDrugsSinceLastCollect won't revert) is allowed only when initialized is true; we assert that seedMarket leaves the contract able to accept a buyDrugs call without reverting on initialized check.
After seeding an empty market (marketDrugs == 0), the contract remains initialized so a subsequent call that requires initialized (getFreeKilo) does not revert.

After seeding the market (first call to seedMarket), the contract's initialized flag is set to true for all inputs on the reference implementation, whereas the mutant leaves initialized false for at least some inputs (so initialized differs between implementations).
After seeding the market with nonzero drugs (when market was zero) the contract becomes initialized=true and marketDrugs equals the seeded amount.
After calling seedMarket(drugs, {value: eth}) when marketDrugs was zero and caller had enough balance, the contract's initialized becomes true and marketDrugs equals the provided drugs.
After calling seedMarket with given drugs and value eth when marketDrugs is zero, the contract becomes initialized and marketDrugs equals the provided drugs.
After calling seedMarket with some drugs and ether amount when marketDrugs is initially zero, the contract should become initialized and marketDrugs should equal the provided drugs.
After calling seedMarket(drugs) with the test contract sending eth, the contract should have initialized == true and marketDrugs == drugs.

For any caller, invoking DrugDealer() always sets ceoAddress to msg.sender (so subsequent seedMarket() call by that ceo can set initialized=true); the mutant breaks this because seedMarket no longer sets initialized=true, so initialized may remain false after the sequence, making the invariant 'if caller called DrugDealer(), then c.ceoAddress()==caller implies c.initialized()==true after seedMarket by that ceo' false for some inputs.
Calling seedMarket when marketDrugs==0 results in initialized becoming true (i.e., seedMarket sets initialized to true).
Calling seedMarket succeeds (does not revert) whenever marketDrugs is zero.
Calling seedMarket(...) when marketDrugs is zero does not revert (i.e., original allows successful seeding), so for any input the call should succeed and reverted must be false.
Only the current ceoAddress can change ceoAddress via DrugDealer() (i.e., after calling DrugDealer(), c.ceoAddress() equals the previous ceoAddress).
Only the current CEO can call DrugDealer to set ceoAddress to themselves (i.e., calling DrugDealer by the current ceoAddress does not revert and results in ceoAddress == msg.sender).
Calling DrugDealer as the current CEO always reverts (original) — so the test asserts that when caller equals c.ceoAddress the call must revert.

If the caller is equal to C.ceoAddress then calling DrugDealer must NOT succeed (i.e., must revert == false), while if the caller is different it must revert in the original — therefore assert that DrugDealer does not succeed when caller != ceoAddress.
Only a caller equal to the current ceoAddress is allowed to invoke DrugDealer successfully (call succeeds iff caller == ceoAddress).
